hint.text: Adages and proverbs use figurative language to express a widely accepted statement about life.
hint.label: Adages & Proverbs

instruction.text: Match the adages and proverbs with their meaning.

atoms.b: It’s better to be or do something late than to never arrive or do something at all.

atoms.a: You can’t have your cake and eat it too.
atoms.b: You need to make a choice, because you can’t have it both ways.

atoms.a: The best things in life are free.
atoms.b: The most valuable things in life do not cost money.

instruction.text: Match the adages and proverbs with their meaning.

atoms.b: Make use of an opportunity quickly.

atoms.a: The grass is always greener on the other side.
atoms.b: The things we don’t have seem better than the things we do have.

atoms.a: You can’t teach an old dog new tricks.
atoms.b: You can’t make people change their behaviour or habits.

instruction.text: Read the scenario and then select the adage or proverb that fits best.

atoms.a: Am I too old to learn how to ride a bike?
b: The grass is always greener on the other side.
You can’t have your cake and eat it too.

atoms.a: Andre wishes his hair was curly instead of straight.
b: Strike while the iron is hot.
You can’t teach an old dog new tricks.
++The grass is always greener on the other side.

atoms.a: They are upset because they want to see a film tonight, but it starts at the same time as the concert.
b: The best things in life are free.
++You can’t have your cake and eat it too.

instruction.text: Fill in the missing words to complete the adage or proverb.

atoms.b: The ((--sky grass --bass)) is always ((--bluer greener --greater)) on the other side.
You ((--can can’t --shouldn’t)) have your ((--coffee cake --shake)) and ((--drink eat --have)) it too.
